messages:
Maya: ok team — quick thread for the webinar on May 6. we need a tight benchmark narrative + battlecard claims + inbound routing rules. goal: ship a launch post + 1-pager + webinar slide deck. final claim set by EOD Thursday pls.

Jia: +1. what are the non-negotiable claims?

Maya: non-negotiables we discussed: 1) predictable per-token cost w/ reserved vs burst tiers, 2) 95th-pct latency SLO comparison (focus on tail), 3) graceful fallbacks to lower-cost model variants when capacity is constrained, 4) unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. keep language concrete, not fuzzy.

Noah: can we call out a concrete bench stat? e.g., "~2x lower 95th-pct latency vs X on typical chat workloads" — legal will want the dataset and test harness.

Deborah: yes please include test harness details. we need a methods appendix for any public claim (datasets, sequence length, batching config, model names). legal sign-off required before press.

Sam: I'll own the benchmark appendix + visuals. plan: run suites today/tomorrow and produce a small graph showing tail latency vs request rate.

Caleb: for messaging, we should frame as "predictable performance at scale" not "faster" — that maps better to infra buyers. but have a separate soundbite for developer docs that highlights latency numbers.

Ellie: working on the webinar deck outline. can we get 3 one-liner battlecard claims per competitor: cloud AI platform, LLM API provider, inference infra vendor? short bullets for SDRs.

Maya: yes — example structure: competitor -> typical customer pain -> our counterclaim + proof artifact (bench, case, quote). short, scannable.

Jia: drafting a quick competitor matrix. rough first pass:
- Cloud AI platforms: strong mgmt + models but variable tail latency under mixed tenants -> claim: "Dedicated SLOs and fallback policies reduce outage risk"
- LLM APIs: easiest to integrate but opaque economics -> claim: "Transparent per-token economics + caching/quantization controls"
- Infra vendors: high control but ops burden -> claim: "Unified runtime + managed rollout reduces infra debt"

Noah: routing question — how do we map inbound leads from the webinar to SDR/AE queues? want automatic routing by intent and company size.

Maya: suggested 3-tier routing:
```
if (intent == "pilot" && company_size >= 1000) -> AE-enterprise
else if (intent == "pooled-prod" || usage_estimate > 500k_tokens/mo) -> SDR-dedicated
else -> self-serve-nurture
```
Use form hidden fields: intent, company_size, usage_estimate.

Caleb: also add a "compliance/regulatory" flag to route private deployment requests to solutions engineering.

Ellie: for webinar CTAs: 1) demo request -> routes per rules above, 2) download bench + ppg -> self-serve nurture, 3) talk to sales -> direct AE. keep CTAs explicit.

Deborah: once claims are drafted, please ping legal in #eng-legal. also avoid comparative language like "X can't" — use neutral contrast phrasing.

Sam: finish update — I kicked off bench run with: 8k concurrent reqs, seq len 512, batching policy optimized. expecting charts by EOD tomorrow. will add methodology into appendix JSON blob.

Maya: good. next: the launch post. tone: engineering-first, with a concise lead: "How we keep inference predictable and cheap at 95th percentile". include CTA to webinar and benchmark download.

Jia: subject line A/B ideas for email/webinar invite:
A) "Reduce inference surprises: live benchmark + playbook"
B) "How to keep LLM latency predictable at scale (bench + slides)"
which is more punchy?

Caleb: B is clearer. A feels fluffy.

Ellie: I'll build the registration page and wire the form fields for routing. need final CTA copy by Wednesday.

Noah: can we get a 1-page battlecard for SDRs with objection handlers? example: 
Q: "Why not just use public API?"
A: "Public APIs are easy but create hidden costs and variability; Redwood offers reserve/burst controls + cost breakdowns per token and per-route."

Maya: yes — keep those <30 words each. include 3 prioritized objections: cost surprise, tail latency, vendor lock-in.

Deborah: send any competitor screenshots or quoted language to legal. also flag any paid benchmark comparisons — we need to disclose tools used.

OpsBot: deploy-note: landing page form -> zapier -> routing lambda deploy queued for 2026-04-05 16:00 UTC. ensure field mapping matches final schema.

Sam: quick note on visuals — prefer a single combined chart showing cost vs latency tradeoff across vendors plus a small table for SLOs. will demo mock tomorrow.

Maya: owners recap:
- Bench & appendix: Sam
- Webinar deck + CTAs: Ellie
- Competitor claims + battlecard bullets: Jia + Caleb
- Legal coordination: Deborah
- Routing implementation: Noah + OpsBot
Everyone: please drop your final text into this thread by EOD Thursday. I'll consolidate and run a final review Friday AM. :rocket:

Caleb: noted. will push concise bullets by Thursday noon.

Deborah: will review claims same day. if anything escalates, I'll ping ops for takedown window.

Maya: thanks all — short and focused. we'll iterate but keep the public claims tight.
